# Component reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm docs:components` from apps/playground/src/catalog and the lab registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every component is exported from `@toyo-ui/react` and needs `ToyoThemeProvider` from `@toyo-ui/theme` at the app root.
The interactive version of this reference is the Component Lab (`pnpm dev`).

## Button

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Buttons

Triggers an action or navigation. Four semantic variants express emphasis; a built-in loading state covers async actions without layout shift.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from '@toyo-ui/react';
import AddIcon from '@mui/icons-material/Add';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Button startIcon={<AddIcon />} onClick={() => console.log('clicked')}>
      Create Component
    </Button>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop              | Type                                                   | Default     | Description                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`         | `'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'outline' \| 'text'`      | `'primary'` | Visual emphasis. Use one primary action per view.                                                                 |
| `size`            | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'`                       | `'medium'`  | Control height: 32 / 40 / 48px.                                                                                   |
| `loading`         | `boolean`                                              | `false`     | Shows a spinner and disables the button; the label stays for a stable accessible name.                            |
| `loadingPosition` | `'start' \| 'center' \| 'end'`                         | `'start'`   | Where the spinner appears. 'center' hides the label visually (it stays available to assistive tech).              |
| `disabled`        | `boolean`                                              | `false`     | Removes the button from the tab order. Prefer explaining why an action is unavailable.                            |
| `fullWidth`       | `boolean`                                              | `false`     | Stretches to the container width.                                                                                 |
| `startIcon`       | `ReactNode`                                            | —           | Icon before the label. Decorative; the label provides the name.                                                   |
| `endIcon`         | `ReactNode`                                            | —           | Icon after the label, e.g. a forward arrow.                                                                       |
| `href`            | `string`                                               | —           | Renders a link styled as a button, using the theme's `linkComponent` (e.g. a router link) when one is configured. |
| `onClick`         | `(event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void` | —           | Click handler. Not called while disabled or loading.                                                              |

**Variants and states:** Default, Hover, Focus-visible, Active, Disabled, Loading, Long content.

### API decisions

- Replaces MUI's `variant` × `color` matrix with four semantic variants, so 'secondary' means the same thing everywhere.
- Removes `disableElevation`, `disableRipple` and `loadingIndicator`: elevation and feedback are design-system decisions, not per-instance ones.
- Keeps every other MUI prop (`href`, `type`, `aria-*`, `onClick`…) through `Omit<MuiButtonProps, …>`, so it remains a drop-in button.
- Defaults `loadingPosition` to 'start' (MUI defaults to 'center', which hides the label) so users still see what is in progress.
- Forwards its ref, so it works with tooltips, menus and focus management.

### Accessibility

- Renders a native &lt;button&gt; (or &lt;a&gt; with href), so Enter and Space work without extra code.
- Icon-only usage must pass `aria-label`; icons next to a visible label are decorative.
- Loading keeps the label and sets aria-busy; the spinner is a progressbar labelled by the button.
- Focus-visible shows the global 2px focus ring with at least 3:1 contrast against the surface.
- Disabled buttons cannot receive focus. When users need to know why, show the reason as text nearby.
- Minimum target height is 32px (small), above the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/Button.test.tsx`)

- Calls onClick on click and on Enter/Space.
- Does not call onClick when disabled or loading.
- Exposes aria-busy and keeps its accessible name while loading.
- Renders a link when href is set.
- Has no axe violations in each variant.

## TextField

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Inputs

Collects short free-form text. The label is mandatory, errors are linked to the input, and validation runs at a predictable moment (blur) instead of on every keystroke.

```tsx
import { TextField } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { TextField } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <TextField
      label="Email address"
      helperText="We'll only use this for build notifications."
      placeholder="name@company.com"
      type="email"
      required
      validate={(v) => (/^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(v) ? undefined : 'Enter a valid email address.')}
      onChange={setEmail}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop               | Type                                                        | Default    | Description                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`                                                    | —          | Accessible name. Required even when visually hidden.                                           |
| `hideLabel`        | `boolean`                                                   | `false`    | Hides the label visually; it stays the accessible name.                                        |
| `helperText`       | `string`                                                    | —          | Hint under the field, linked via aria-describedby. Replaced by the error when present.         |
| `errorMessage`     | `string`                                                    | —          | Error to show. Its presence sets aria-invalid. Overrides `validate`.                           |
| `validate`         | `(value: string) => string \| undefined`                    | —          | Runs on blur, then on each change once an error is showing. Return a message to show an error. |
| `onChange`         | `(value: string) => void`                                   | —          | Receives the new string value, not the event.                                                  |
| `value`            | `string`                                                    | —          | Controlled value. Omit for uncontrolled use with `defaultValue`.                               |
| `required`         | `boolean`                                                   | `false`    | Marks the field required (native attribute and visual asterisk).                               |
| `size`             | `'small' \| 'medium'`                                       | `'medium'` | Control height: 32 / 40px.                                                                     |
| `maxLength`        | `number`                                                    | —          | Enforced character limit with a live "n / max" counter.                                        |
| `startIcon`        | `ReactNode`                                                 | —          | Decorative icon inside the start of the field.                                                 |
| `type`             | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'password' \| 'search' \| 'url' \| …` | `'text'`   | Native input type.                                                                             |

**Variants and states:** Default, Focus-visible, Filled, Disabled, Error, Required, With counter, Hidden label.

### API decisions

- `label` is required at the type level — the most common accessibility failure for inputs becomes a compile error.
- Replaces MUI's `error` + `helperText` pair with `errorMessage`: one source of truth, so an error can't be flagged without saying what is wrong.
- `onChange` receives the string value; consumers don't unwrap `event.target.value` everywhere.
- Omits `select` and `multiline`: those deserve their own components with their own accessibility contracts.
- Validation is a pure function prop rather than a form library integration, so it works with any form state.

### Accessibility

- The label is a real &lt;label&gt; associated with the input; `hideLabel` keeps it in the accessibility tree.
- Helper text and errors are linked through aria-describedby and read after the label.
- Error state sets aria-invalid="true"; the message says how to fix the problem, not just that it is wrong.
- Validation waits for blur, so screen-reader users are not interrupted while typing.
- The character counter is a polite live region and includes "characters used" for context.
- Placeholder text is never used as a label substitute.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/TextField.test.tsx`)

- Input is reachable by role and accessible name.
- Helper text is the accessible description.
- validate runs on blur, sets aria-invalid and the error description, and clears as the value is fixed.
- errorMessage overrides validate.
- onChange receives strings; controlled values are respected.
- maxLength is enforced and the counter updates.
- No axe violations in the error state.

## Alert

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Feedback

Communicates the outcome of an action or a condition that needs attention, inline with the content it relates to. The screen-reader behavior follows the message's urgency.

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { Alert, Button } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Alert
      severity="warning"
      title="Revision pending review"
      onClose={() => setVisible(false)}
      action={
        <Button size="small" variant="outline">
          Review
        </Button>
      }
    >
      Button v2.3 changes the default loading position. Review the migration notes before release.
    </Alert>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop                  | Type                                          | Default  | Description                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `severity`            | `'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | `'info'` | Tone, icon and live-region role.                                               |
| `title`               | `string`                                      | —        | Short bold summary above the message.                                          |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode`                                   | —        | The message.                                                                   |
| `onClose`             | `() => void`                                  | —        | Shows a close button labelled "Dismiss".                                       |
| `action`              | `ReactNode`                                   | —        | Extra action at the end, e.g. a Retry button.                                  |
| `announce`            | `boolean`                                     | `true`   | false removes the live-region role for messages that are present on page load. |

**Variants and states:** Info, Success, Warning, Error, With title, With action, Dismissible, Long content.

### API decisions

- Maps severity to the ARIA role: error/warning → role="alert" (assertive), info/success → role="status" (polite). MUI uses role="alert" for everything, which interrupts users for routine confirmations.
- `announce={false}` covers static alerts; MUI offers no first-class way to opt out of the live region.
- Removes MUI's `variant` (standard/filled/outlined) and `color`: Toyo-ui has one alert style built on the contrast-tested tonal tokens.
- The close button is labelled "Dismiss" instead of MUI's "Close".

### Accessibility

- Errors and warnings use role="alert" and are announced immediately; info and success use role="status" and wait for a pause.
- Render the alert container before inserting the message when possible; live regions added with content already inside may not be announced by every screen reader.
- The icon is decorative; severity is also conveyed by the title or message text, never by color alone.
- Body text uses text.primary on the tonal background (≥ 4.5:1, enforced by token tests).
- The dismiss button has an accessible name and is reachable by keyboard.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/Alert.test.tsx`)

- Each severity renders the expected role (alert vs status).
- announce={false} removes the live role.
- Title renders; the dismiss button is labelled and calls onClose.
- No axe violations for each severity.

## StatusBadge

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Feedback

Shows the state of a record (approved, failing, draft…) in tables, headers and lists with one shared color language.

```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  return <StatusBadge tone="success" label="Approved" />;
}
```

### Props

| Prop               | Type                                                       | Default   | Description                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tone` (required)  | `'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'info' \| 'neutral'` | —         | Semantic tone. Shared with Alert.                                |
| `label` (required) | `string`                                                   | —         | Visible text. Always rendered so color is never the only signal. |
| `size`             | `'small' \| 'medium'`                                      | `'small'` | 22 / 28px height.                                                |
| `showDot`          | `boolean`                                                  | `true`    | Leading decorative dot.                                          |

**Variants and states:** Success, Warning, Error, Info, Neutral, Without dot, Medium size.

### API decisions

- Built on a &lt;span&gt;, not MUI `Chip`: a badge is not interactive, and Chip brings click/delete semantics that would need to be suppressed.
- `tone` + required `label` instead of a color prop — product code says what the state means, the library decides how it looks.
- Tones are shared with Alert through a single `StatusTone` type and `TONE_COLORS` map.

### Accessibility

- The label is real text, so status is available without color (WCAG 1.4.1).
- The dot is aria-hidden.
- Not a live region: if a status changes in response to user action, announce the change with an Alert or status message.
- Tone text on tonal background meets 4.5:1 in both schemes (token tests).

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/StatusBadge.test.tsx`)

- Every tone renders its label as visible text.
- The dot is hidden from assistive technology and optional.
- It is not a live region.
- No axe violations across tones.

## LoadingState

**Status:** beta · **Category:** Feedback

Tells users that content or an operation is in progress, with a label that assistive technology announces once.

```tsx
import { LoadingState } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { LoadingState } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  return <LoadingState variant="linear" label="Loading components" progress={64} />;
}
```

### Props

| Prop        | Type                                  | Default     | Description                                                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `'spinner' \| 'linear' \| 'skeleton'` | `'spinner'` | Spinner for short waits, linear for progress, skeleton for content placeholders. |
| `label`     | `string`                              | `'Loading'` | What is loading. Announced and, unless hidden, visible.                          |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean`                             | `false`     | Hides the label visually only.                                                   |
| `progress`  | `number`                              | —           | 0–100 for determinate progress (clamped). Omit when unknown.                     |
| `lines`     | `number`                              | `3`         | Placeholder lines for the skeleton variant.                                      |

**Variants and states:** Spinner, Linear indeterminate, Linear determinate, Skeleton, Hidden label.

### API decisions

- One component for three MUI primitives (CircularProgress, LinearProgress, Skeleton) so every loading state gets the same announcement behavior.
- `label` defaults to "Loading" — MUI progress indicators have no accessible name by default.
- Progress is clamped to 0–100 so bad input never produces invalid aria-valuenow.

### Accessibility

- Wrapped in role="status" so the label is announced politely once.
- Spinner and bar are progressbars named by the label; determinate progress exposes aria-valuenow.
- Skeletons set aria-busy and hide the placeholder shapes from assistive technology.
- Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion through the global theme rule.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/LoadingState.test.tsx`)

- Each variant is announced with its label.
- Determinate progress exposes aria-valuenow and visible percentage.
- Progress is clamped.
- Skeleton is busy and renders the requested lines.
- No axe violations with a hidden label.

## EmptyState

**Status:** beta · **Category:** Feedback

Explains why there is nothing to show and offers the next step, instead of leaving a blank area.

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  return (
    <EmptyState
      kind="no-results"
      title="No components match your filters"
      description="Try removing a filter or searching by component name."
      action={
        <Button variant="outline" onClick={clearFilters}>
          Clear filters
        </Button>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop               | Type                                   | Default     | Description                               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `title` (required) | `string`                               | —           | What is empty.                            |
| `description`      | `string`                               | —           | Why, and how to get content.              |
| `kind`             | `'no-data' \| 'no-results' \| 'error'` | `'no-data'` | Chooses the default icon.                 |
| `icon`             | `ReactNode`                            | —           | Overrides the default icon. Decorative.   |
| `action`           | `ReactNode`                            | —           | Recovery action, e.g. "Clear filters".    |
| `size`             | `'compact' \| 'default'`               | `'default'` | Compact for use inside tables and panels. |

**Variants and states:** No data, No results, Error, With action, Compact.

### API decisions

- No MUI equivalent; composed from Box and Typography.
- `kind` encodes the three reasons a view is empty so teams use consistent icons and wording.
- The title is not a heading: empty states appear inside sections that already have one.

### Accessibility

- role="status" announces the empty state when a filter or search produces it.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- The action is a real button or link with a descriptive label.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/EmptyState.test.tsx`)

- Title and description are announced as a status.
- The action is operable.
- It renders no heading.
- No axe violations.

## Dialog

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Overlays

Interrupts the flow to confirm a consequential action or collect a small amount of focused input.

```tsx
import { Dialog } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { Button, Dialog } from '@toyo-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';

export function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open dialog</Button>
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Delete component?"
        description="This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete the component and all of its variants."
        confirmLabel="Delete"
        tone="destructive"
        onConfirm={async () => {
          await deleteComponent();
          setOpen(false);
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop                 | Type                                                   | Default         | Description                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open` (required)    | `boolean`                                              | —               | Visibility.                                                                             |
| `onClose` (required) | `(reason: 'escape' \| 'backdrop' \| 'cancel') => void` | —               | Called on Escape, backdrop click or Cancel. Never called while a confirm is pending.    |
| `title` (required)   | `string`                                               | —               | Dialog name (aria-labelledby). Phrase as a question for confirmations.                  |
| `description`        | `ReactNode`                                            | —               | Consequences (aria-describedby).                                                        |
| `children`           | `ReactNode`                                            | —               | Extra content such as a short form.                                                     |
| `onConfirm`          | `() => void \| Promise<void>`                          | —               | Shows the confirm button. A returned promise keeps the dialog loading until it settles. |
| `confirmLabel`       | `string`                                               | `'Confirm'`     | Use a verb that names the action ("Delete").                                            |
| `cancelLabel`        | `string`                                               | `'Cancel'`      | Safe action.                                                                            |
| `tone`               | `'default' \| 'destructive'`                           | `'default'`     | Destructive adds a warning icon, danger-toned confirm and focuses Cancel first.         |
| `loading`            | `boolean`                                              | `false`         | Controlled loading, combined with the promise-driven state.                             |
| `size`               | `'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large'`                       | `'small'`       | Max width: 444 / 600 / 900px.                                                           |
| `container`          | `HTMLElement \| null`                                  | `document.body` | Portal target. Render inside a scoped theme or color scheme, or a shadow root.          |

**Variants and states:** Default, Destructive, Loading (async confirm), With content, Sizes.

### API decisions

- Composes MUI Dialog, DialogTitle, DialogContent and DialogActions into one component with a confirm/cancel contract — the common case needs no assembly.
- `onClose` receives a typed reason ('escape' | 'backdrop' | 'cancel') instead of MUI's event + string.
- `onConfirm` may return a promise; the dialog owns the pending state, disables Cancel and ignores Escape/backdrop until it settles, preventing double submits and lost requests.
- Initial focus follows the WAI-ARIA pattern: Cancel for destructive dialogs, Confirm otherwise. Applied after the enter transition, not with autoFocus, and never overrides focus the user has already moved into the dialog.

### Accessibility

- role="dialog" with aria-modal, named by the title and described by the description.
- Focus moves into the dialog on open, is trapped while open, and returns to the trigger on close (MUI focus trap).
- Escape closes the dialog unless a confirm is pending.
- Destructive dialogs focus the least destructive action first.
- If the user starts typing in a field before the enter transition ends, focus stays in that field.
- The pending confirm button keeps its label and exposes aria-busy.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/Dialog.test.tsx`)

- Labelled by title and described by description.
- Escape and Cancel call onClose with the right reason.
- Initial focus: Cancel when destructive, Confirm otherwise.
- Does not steal focus from a field the user is already typing in.
- Async confirm shows loading, disables Cancel and blocks Escape until it resolves.
- Focus stays inside while tabbing.
- No axe violations.

## DataTable

**Status:** stable · **Category:** Data Display

Displays records with a few comparable attributes, sortable by column, with consistent loading and empty states.

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@toyo-ui/react';
```

### Usage

```tsx
import { DataTable, StatusBadge } from '@toyo-ui/react';
import type { Column } from '@toyo-ui/react';

export function Example() {
  const columns: Column<ComponentRow>[] = [
    { key: 'name', header: 'Component', render: (r) => r.name, sortValue: (r) => r.name },
    { key: 'tests', header: 'Tests', align: 'right', render: (r) => r.tests, sortValue: (r) => r.tests },
    { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (r) => <StatusBadge tone={r.status.tone} label={r.status.label} /> },
  ];

  return (
    <DataTable caption="Library components" showCaption columns={columns} rows={components} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Prop                  | Type                                          | Default     | Description                                                                      |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `caption` (required)  | `string`                                      | —           | Accessible table name, rendered as &lt;caption&gt; (visually hidden by default). |
| `showCaption`         | `boolean`                                     | `false`     | Shows the caption visually.                                                      |
| `columns` (required)  | `Column<T>[]`                                 | —           | { key, header, render(row), sortValue?(row), align?, width?, hideOnMobile? }     |
| `rows` (required)     | `T[]`                                         | —           | Row data. The row type flows into every column renderer.                         |
| `getRowId` (required) | `(row: T) => string`                          | —           | Stable React key.                                                                |
| `onRowClick`          | `(row: T) => void`                            | —           | Row click handler. Also put a link or button in a cell for keyboard users.       |
| `initialSort`         | `{ key: string; direction: 'asc' \| 'desc' }` | —           | Initial sort.                                                                    |
| `loading`             | `boolean`                                     | `false`     | Skeleton rows and aria-busy.                                                     |
| `density`             | `'compact' \| 'comfortable'`                  | `'compact'` | Row height.                                                                      |
| `emptyState`          | `ReactNode`                                   | —           | Replaces the default EmptyState.                                                 |

**Variants and states:** Default, Sorted asc/desc, Loading, Empty, Clickable rows, Comfortable density, Mobile (hidden columns).

### API decisions

- Generic over the row type: `DataTable<Part>` type-checks every `render` and `sortValue` at the call site.
- Declarative columns instead of composing MUI Table* primitives by hand on every screen.
- `sortValue` returns numbers for numeric sort, so "10" never sorts before "9".
- `onRowClick` instead of a router-specific href: the library doesn't depend on the app's router.
- No pagination or virtualization yet — appropriate up to a few hundred rows (documented limitation).

### Accessibility

- A real &lt;table&gt; with &lt;caption&gt;, column headers and cells — screen readers announce headers as users move between cells.
- Sortable headers are buttons and expose aria-sort on the header cell.
- Loading sets aria-busy on the table; skeleton rows are aria-hidden.
- Row click is a convenience only: keyboard users need a link or button inside the row.
- hideOnMobile removes secondary columns below 900px rather than forcing horizontal scrolling.

### Test coverage (`packages/react/src/DataTable.test.tsx`)

- Caption names the table; headers and rows render.
- Clicking a header sorts and sets aria-sort; second click reverses.
- Empty rows show the empty state.
- Loading sets aria-busy and hides data.
- onRowClick receives the row.
- No axe violations.
